transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what finally got me to come in is that I just don’t seem to care about the things that used to help me feel normal. I used to do sailing races, volunteer at the historical society on Saturdays, spend time in my woodshop… and now all of that just feels like a chore. I keep putting it off, and that’s not really like me.
Have you noticed if this lack of interest in your usual activities is accompanied by feeling down or sad most of the time?

I wouldn’t say I’m sad all the time exactly. It’s more like this low-grade dread that’s just there, and a lot of guilt. Like I keep thinking I should’ve seen one more risk coming, even though people tell me the controls were in place. It just follows me around.
Have you noticed a decreased ability to experience pleasure from activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes. That’s probably the biggest change I’ve noticed. Sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, working in the woodshop—those used to keep me balanced. Now they just feel like chores, and I keep putting them off.
Have you noticed that you feel fatigued or that you’ve lost your energy a lot of the time, even when you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

I don’t think so, not in a clear way. I mean, I get tired like anyone does, but I haven’t really noticed a big loss of energy when I haven’t done much. It’s more that I have trouble getting myself to start things.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even simple ones, lately?

Yes, sometimes. It’s not constant, but out of nowhere I’ll suddenly see that scaffold dropping in my head, really clearly, like a photo. If I hear metal clank or a backup alarm, that can set it off, and then for a few minutes I have a hard time staying with whatever meeting or conversation I’m actually in.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately?
Not really. My appetite seems about the same, and I haven’t noticed any weight change that stands out.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like trouble falling asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than usual and not being able to go back to sleep?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Most nights I can fall asleep at a normal time, but then I wake up around two or three in the morning. My mind goes right back to that job site, and after that I’m just lying there kind of on alert, listening for every little sound. It doesn’t feel like I’m getting real rest after that.
Have you had experiences like this before, where your mood was low and you lost interest in things, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I don’t remember feeling like this before, not in this way. What finally made me agree to come in is that I just don’t care about things that used to keep me steady—sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society, even messing around in the woodshop. They all just feel like chores now, and I keep putting them off.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this one where you felt this way—losing interest in things and feeling down— or is this truly the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

Yeah… like I said, I don’t really remember going through this before. This feels new to me. The thing that pushed me to come in is that I just don’t care about the things that used to keep me balanced—sailing, my Saturday historical society shift, working in the woodshop. Now they just feel like chores, and I keep putting them off.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the loss of interest in activities and the low mood?
It’s been a little over a year, I think. It started after the scaffold accident, during that whole business readjustment period, and it just kind of stuck around since then.
